title: Wave-based release scheduler and notes synchronizer
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Design and implement a 'wave scheduler' that replaces the brittle single-cut weekly process with managed waves (canary -> regional -> global) and a paired Release Notes Synchronizer that auto-generates structured release notes aligned to each wave. The scheduler will: 1) group commits into candidate waves based on branch / tag patterns and semantic bump intent, 2) create RC tags with build metadata, 3) orchestrate canary cohorts and timed promotions, and 4) emit machine-readable release metadata consumed by Console, Upgrade Assistant, and the release-notes generator. The release notes synchronizer will parse commit messages, PR titles, and linked JIRA/Linear tickets, apply conventional-commit heuristics and an ML summarizer fallback for multi-PR features, and produce both human prose and structured changelog sections (security, breaking changes, user-visible enhancements, infra/ops notes).
acceptance_criteria: Wave scheduler produces rc tags named r{major}.{minor}.{patch}-rc{wave}+{buildmeta} and records wave metadata in /release-metadata/{tag}.json
Automated release notes show up in the Console draft notes panel within 10 minutes of an RC tag being created
Canary promotion automation can execute staged traffic switches and rollback if gate thresholds (error-rate, p99 latency, failed transactions) are violated
Upgrade Assistant can read release metadata, present a per-wave risk summary, and precipitate recommended steps for private deployments
End-to-end test: create a test branch, produce an RC wave, simulate canary metrics; scheduler promotes to regional wave after 24h with health gates satisfied
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 0-2): Implement tagging and metadata emitter. Disable automatic promotions; scheduler only creates RC tags and metadata.
Phase 2 (Week 2-4): Enable notes synchronizer to generate draft notes and post to Console. Add human review step (PM/Docs).
Phase 3 (Week 4-6): Wire canary promotion automation with metric gates; run internal dogfooding on staging clusters.
Phase 4 (Week 6-8): Gradual enablement on production for low-risk services with 10% traffic canaries, expand to global after 48h of stability.
automation_notes: Tagging logic: semantic intent extracted from PR labels and conventional-commit footer (BREAKING CHANGE => major bump). If multiple bump intents exist, highest precedence applies.
Release metadata includes: commits[], prs[], author_map, estimated_risk_score, canary_cohort, gate_rules
Release notes composer pipeline: commit->PR->ticket mapping -> conventional-parser -> bulletize -> ML-summarizer fallback -> human edit -> publish
All automation steps log to release-orchestrator stream (kafka) for observability and replay
qa_plan: Unit tests for tag generation, bump precedence, and metadata schema validation
Integration tests: simulate CI producing RC tag and ensure Console picks up draft notes
Chaos tests: intentionally flip a canary cohort to error state and assert rollback triggers
Manual review checklist for the first three production waves (PM, Docs, SRE signoff)
